Question: Which AWS compute service is serverless?
Answer Status / Notes: A: Correct; B: Your answer, Incorrect; C and D: would be incorrect.
Explanation A: Lambda is a serverless service. When you use Lambda, you upload code and choose an event that will determine when the function runs. AWS manages all the patches, infrastructure maintenance, and capacity planning of Lambda.
Explanation B: Amazon EC2 is not a serverless service. Amazon EC2 provides secure, resizable compute capacity in the cloud. When you provision an EC2 instance, you have access to the EC2 instance and operating system to implement patches or maintenance tasks. When you use Amazon EC2, you must implement infrastructure management tasks like capacity provisioning.
Explanation C: Amazon ECS is not a serverless service in all use cases. Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service that gives you the ability to run containers on various platforms. You can run the containers on an Amazon EC2 based compute platform, on external instances, or on an AWS Fargate serverless compute platform. With Amazon EC2 based compute clusters as the host platform, you must manage the compute cluster that the containers are hosted on. This use case requires you to manage capacity planning and patching tasks. Therefore, in this use case, Amazon ECS is not serverless.
Explanation D: Amazon RDS is not a serverless service. Amazon RDS runs a database engine on top of DB instances. When you create a database by using Amazon RDS, you must first select the DB instance size and type as part of the capacity planning process. Then, as the Amazon RDS storage or usage capacity gets consumed, you must implement capacity provisioning and management tasks. AWS does not automatically handle the capacity and management tasks.

Explanation D: Security groups are used to manage traffic from specific IP addresses or ranges to specific ports. Security groups do not mitigate against SQL injection attacks.

Question:
A company has existing software licenses that it wants to bring to AWS, but the licensing model requires licensing physical cores.
How can the company meet this requirement in the AWS Cloud?
Option A: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance on a Dedicated Host.
Option D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance with default tenancy.
Answer Status / Notes: A: Your answer, Correct; B, C and D: would be incorrect.
Explanation A: A Dedicated Host can isolate EC2 instances from other accounts. You can control portions of the physical layer. Dedicated Hosts give you the ability to use existing software licenses.
Explanation B: You can reserve a set number of On-Demand EC2 instances with shared tenancy in an Availability Zone. This solution makes On-Demand EC2 instances available when needed. However, a solution that creates an On-Demand Capacity Reservation would not meet the requirement of licensing physical cores.
Explanation C: Dedicated Reserved Instances give you the ability to launch an EC2 instance on a physical server that is isolated from other accounts. The account user must commit for 1 year or 3 years. Dedicated Reserved Instances do not give you the ability to control the physical layer of the instance.
Explanation D: Default tenancy automatically applies to an EC2 instance that you launch on demand. AWS places the EC2 instance on physical hardware that you share with other accounts. You have no control of the physical layer. Therefore, you would not be able to use the existing software license on the physical cores.
Learn More B: Learn more about On-Demand Capacity Reservations .

Question:
A user needs to perform a one-time backup of an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is attached to an Amazon EC2 instance.
What is the MOST operationally efficient way to perform this backup?
Option A: Copy the EBS volume to a server that is running outside AWS and is connected with AWS Direct Connect.
Option B: Create a custom script to copy the EBS file contents to Amazon S3.
Option C: Create an EBS snapshot of the volume.
Option D: Attach another EBS volume to the EC2 instance, and copy the contents.
Answer Status / Notes: C: Correct; B: Your answer, Incorrect; A and D: would be incorrect.
Explanation A: You can use Direct Connect to connect an internal network to the AWS Cloud through an Ethernet fiber-optic cable. You can copy an EBS volume to an external server over Direct Connect. However, this approach is not the most operationally efficient way to perform the backup. This approach requires additional infrastructure and complex data transfer processes. This approach is both time-consuming and resource-intensive.
Explanation B: You can create and maintain a custom script to copy contents to Amazon S3. However, this approach requires development effort, testing, and ongoing maintenance. This approach is not as operationally efficient as using a built-in capability of Amazon EBS.
Explanation C: An EBS snapshot is a built-in feature that provides a point-in-time backup of an EBS volume. An EBS snapshot requires only a single API call or a single click. Snapshots are incremental. AWS automatically stores EBS snapshots in Amazon S3. You can create an EBS snapshot while the volume is attached and in use. This is the most operationally efficient way to perform a backup because you use built-in AWS functionality with minimal effort.
Explanation D: You can attach another EBS volume and copy the contents. However, this approach requires multiple manual steps. You must attach the new volume, mount the volume, and manage the copy process. This approach is not the most operationally efficient.
